title: Man shot by RCMP was 'agitated' and had a hammer, ASIRT investigators say
subtitle: Nathan Leather, 39, died after altercation with Strathmore RCMP on Christmas Day
article: New details have emerged regarding a fatal police shooting on Christmas Day in Strathmore, Alta.
Nathan Leather, 39, from Siksika Nation died after an altercation with RCMP on Dec. 25.
The incident began late at night with a report of an "agitated man" inside the Husky gas station on Ridge Road.

In a release, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) said surveillance video from inside a store shows two officers arriving at 3:43 a.m. and speaking to him. He remained inside the store. At 4:20 a.m., the officers tried to arrest him.
Police had said the man was carrying a weapon during the confrontation, but the weapon was not identified at the time.
ASIRT has now identified that Leather was holding a hammer and a walking cane.

"The man and the two officers struggled, and the officers used their conducted energy weapons on him. The officers then left the store to await backup. The man remained inside and began to self-harm and damage the store and its contents," ASIRT said in the release.
"By this time, the attendant had left the store and was not in danger."

According to ASIRT, Leather left the store again a few minutes later, encountering additional officers in marked police vehicles who arrived and stopped at the intersection near the gas station at 4:44 a.m.
A confrontation occurred and two of the officers discharged their firearms, striking the man. In a video that circulated online after the incident, what sounded like several shots were audible.
Police said the man was treated by the officers and then emergency medical services. He was taken to hospital, where he died.
Investigators found a hammer near the police vehicles in the intersection.
Family and friends gathered on Dec. 29 for a candlelight vigil to remember Leather. He was described as a husband, a son and a friend to many.
His mother-in-law said he had seven children, including three who were adopted.
During the vigil, Siksika Chief Ouray Crowfoot emphasized that the community needs to respect Leather and the process and see what happens with the investigation.
ASIRT investigates when serious injury or death may have been caused by police. The watchdog agency also investigates credible allegations of police misconduct.
